title: Kyoto Bar Lets Disabled People Work via Robot
paragraphs: A new bar in Kyoto will soon let people who cannot leave their homes work as bartenders, using robots.
The bar, called OrySNACK Kyoto, is being opened by OryLab, a Japanese company that makes avatar robots called OriHime. It is expected to open in December.

The robots in the bar are not controlled by artificial intelligence. Instead, real people control them from their homes. Using a remote control, they can move the robot and talk with customers through its camera and speaker. The controls can even be used by a person lying down.

The bar is designed for people who find it difficult to travel to a normal workplace. This includes people with illnesses and disabilities, such as muscular dystrophy and ALS, as well as people who are pregnant or caring for family members.
OryLab chose Kyoto because many different visitors from Japan and other countries go there. This will give the robot operators the chance to talk with many different kinds of customers.

The Kyoto bar will be OryLab's second "snack bar." A snack bar is a type of small Japanese bar where staff chat with customers. The first one opened in Tokyo's Chuo Ward in August 2026. There, six operators work during each shift, and customers can try different types of sake. About 100 people are registered to work there by controlling robots. One of them is Guro Mama, a 59-year-old woman with muscular dystrophy, who talks about sake with customers from her home.
OryLab has used robots like this before. In 2021, it opened the Avatar Robot Cafe Dawn in Tokyo, which gets about 60,000 visitors a year.
In the future, OryLab hopes that one of its robot operators will run their own bar.
